correctness.rationale: For every \(N\ge3\) and distinct a,b, root-of-unity character orthogonality yields \(S_{\mathrm{full}}=NI/2\) and retained eigenvalues \((N-r\pm|z_E|)/2\). The projection-greedy argument finds the maximal capacity-constrained root sum; strict convexity at tied boundary directions prohibits split partial occupation. All possible maximizing phase-count vectors are precisely consecutive full blocks and a partial adjacent class. Counting their distinct rotations/reflections and labelled choices gives the claimed count formula, and one-ray capacity g gives the exact retained-span cutoff. The standard-library checker ran 635 index parameter cases, 81,920 erasure masks, and 246 independent capacity cases, with max numerical discrepancy about 2.1e-14. This finite test is supplemental; the proof applies to all parameters.

value.rationale: Adversarial erasure stability directly controls reliable recovery from incomplete redundant Fourier measurements. The claim determines the exact worst residual eigenvalue interval for every N, frequency pair, and deletion count, and completely identifies and enumerates the damaging masks. The gcd parameter has a concrete origin in repeated projective sensing directions and quantitatively refines the previously known safety threshold \(N-g-1\). This is a complete natural parametric classification, not a single arbitrary numerical example or a routine renaming of a general frame bound.
